name: Scientific racism
summary: Scientific racism is the belief that humanity divides into biologically distinct races whose hereditary traits justify ranking them and treating them differently. Its classic form (Gobineau, Grant) holds that race drives the rise and fall of civilizations and calls for immigration limits, eugenics and rule by the best-bred; its modern 'race realism' or human biodiversity form stresses genetic group differences in intelligence. Modern science rejects its central claims.
scope: The classic tradition from Gobineau (1853) to Madison Grant (1916) and the eugenics era, plus the modern race-realist or human biodiversity current as described by Wikipedia (Jensen, Rushton, Lynn). It is a set of empirical claims with political implications rather than a full program, so many economic and constitutional answers are low-confidence inferences.

cut-welfare.rationale: Split: Grant attacked charity as preserving inferior stock and some modern proponents oppose equalising programmes, but the strands differ on welfare.

state-harmful.rationale: Grant wants the state to manage breeding, including sterilization, so the state is a useful instrument.

more-religion-public.rationale: Gobineau doubts religion's power and Grant criticizes church influence on breeding.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Proponents deny that group gaps stem from injustice and oppose affirmative action.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Gobineau holds that a people's character, hence its institutions, depends on keeping its original blood.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Grant opposed unrestricted entry and the melting pot, and the movement is documented as a driver of 1920s quota laws.

open-borders.rationale: Grant warned that freedom of entry would swamp the founding stock; open borders is the opposite of the immigration policy the movement advocated.

experts-over-public.rationale: Grant wants government by the wisest and best, and the movement presents itself as science that the public resists.

democracy-best.rationale: Grant says universal suffrage favors the average man over the wisest, and Gobineau says democracy has no root in reality.

direct-votes.rationale: Grant rejects the idea that the voice of the people is the voice of God.

natural-rulers.rationale: Grant says true aristocracy is rule by the wisest and best, a minority selected by birth and breeding; Gobineau ties aristocracy to race.

war-builds-character.rationale: Grant calls war dysgenic because it destroys the best stock.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Gobineau and Grant treat a people's racial stock as the basis of its nation and civilization.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Gobineau holds race overshadows all other questions of history, displacing class as the driver.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Both Gobineau and Grant treat natural inequality between peoples and individuals as fixed, so equalizing outcomes is misguided.

human-enhancement.rationale: The movement is documented as promoting genetic engineering and neo-eugenics.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The defining claim: racial groups differ innately in ability, as Grant, Gobineau and modern race-science writers hold.

national-rebirth.rationale: Grant and Gobineau frame the dominant race as in decline and in need of renewal by protecting its stock.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Presents itself as science rather than faith, though Gobineau and Grant also lean on race mysticism.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Split: classic scientific racism was cited to justify segregation and apartheid, while modern race realists more often favour informal differentiation than formal law.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Grant rejects the melting pot because hereditary traits cannot be changed by environment, so assimilation cannot work.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Grant says the state must see that the lines of the unfit stop through sterilization, and eugenics is documented as a core policy of the tradition.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Gobineau and Grant treat race mixture as the cause of civilizational decline and urge racial separation.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Gobineau and Grant reject equality of races and of persons and rank people by heredity.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Gobineau and Grant reject democracy and favor rule by the racially fit, so consent of the governed is not the ground of authority.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Scientific racism presents itself as objective empirical science and rejects the view that knowledge reflects power; modern race realists attack this claim as censorship.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Gobineau and Grant treat struggle between races as the driver of civilizational rise and fall.

separated-powers.rationale: Classic strands favored rule by the best-bred and modern strands accept liberal constitutions; adherents are split.

vanguard-party.rationale: No stated position; the doctrine is not a class-revolutionary one, and inference from its elitist but non-Marxist frame gives mild disagreement.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Gobineau and Grant hold that race mixture dissolves a people and drives civilizational decline, and the modern strand cites diversity as a source of conflict.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Both Grant and Gobineau reject equality and democracy and want rule by the racially superior, which a lottery among all citizens contradicts.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Its central claim is that races and their civilizations are biologically ranked higher and lower.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Grant wanted the nation held by the old Nordic stock, so membership by descent over birthplace follows directly.

character-from-environment.rationale: Heredity over environment is the defining claim: Grant and Gobineau hold that race and inherited traits, not upbringing, decide character and civilization, and the modern human biodiversity current says the same of intelligence.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Segregationists could accept separate institutions while others want strict exclusion, so adherents split.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Gobineau makes race the key to history and the rise and fall of civilizations, in place of economic or moral causes.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Grant and Gobineau reject democracy and equality and favor rule by the best-bred, so they distrust unchecked majorities and wish institutions to be in elite hands.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Gobineau and Grant favor an aristocracy of the best-bred; modern race realists are less committed to titles.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Grant's tradition is not tied to constitutional design and adherents are divided.

elective-rulers.rationale: Gobineau and Grant rejected democracy and favored rule by the racially best-bred and aristocratic elites over popular election.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: No stated position; Gobineau lamented cultural decline but not through media pacification.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Hereditarians attribute differences between national wealth to inherited group abilities, not to exploitation.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: A racial hierarchy places Europeans above other races and opposes rule by those held to be lower.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Gobineau and Grant hold that race determines a people's institutions and capacity for self-government.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Gobineau and Grant reject democracy and equality and favor rule by a racial elite, so binding delegates to the mass is opposed.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Adherents attribute group outcome gaps to heredity rather than discrimination, so unequal outcomes prove nothing about bias.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Grant and the eugenicists want the fit stock to breed more and immigration cut, which this matches.

industrial-unions.rationale: Labour organisation is outside the sources; adherents are indifferent or split.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Classic writers had antisemitic strands but the modern race-realist current mostly disowns conspiracy claims, so adherents are split.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Eugenic programs depend on the state regulating marriage and breeding, so abolishing legal marriage runs against them.

religious-nation.rationale: The tradition defines community by race and heredity, not by shared religion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Adherents are split: eugenicists saw industrial society as dysgenic, while modern race realists mostly accept markets.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The tradition is not an economic program and adherents split between market, corporatist and elitist views.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Grant and Gobineau distrust mass democracy and favor rule by the best-bred.

racial-franchise.rationale: Split: Grant and the classic tradition backed racially restricted citizenship and franchise, as Wikipedia documents, but modern race realists do not generally call for it.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Gobineau and Grant reject the equality of races and deny that communities share power equally; the tradition favors the dominance of the supposedly superior race.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The sources state nothing about regional administration.

online-anonymity.rationale: Modern human biodiversity writers often use pseudonyms but the sources show no stated position.

person-over-state.rationale: Grant urges that the state sterilize the unfit and subordinates individuals to the quality of the racial stock, so persons may be used for the group's ends.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The tradition's biological determinism is secular, but Gobineau and others invoke spiritual claims; adherents are split.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Grant and Gobineau hold that races have distinct hereditary interests and that the 'Nordic' race should act to protect itself.

racial-pride.rationale: The tradition ranks races and treats the superior race's pride and preservation as justified.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Grant fears immigration swamping the native stock, but the sources describe no plots by foreign powers, so adherents are split.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The tradition has no stated position on fiscal rules; adherents are split across conservative and radical positions.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The tradition has no stated position on the form of the state; classic authors wanted rule by the best-bred but did not call for smashing the state.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Scientific racism holds that humanity divides into biologically distinct races with unequal traits, which contradicts a single shared human nature grounding equal dignity; it also backs eugenic redesign of the stock.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Gobineau and Grant reject democracy and equality in favor of rule by the best-bred, so they would not accept a purely procedural test.

race-social-construct.rationale: Scientific racism holds that races are biologically real and hereditarily different, and modern race realists restate this against the social-construct view.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Race realists hold that group gaps come largely from heredity, so racism is not the main cause of disadvantage.

material-over-identity.rationale: The tradition treats race as primary but gives no view on what the left should do; adherents are split.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Split: Grant attacked charity as preserving inferior stock and some modern proponents oppose equalising programmes, but the strands differ on welfare. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: The state should discourage or prevent people with heritable defects from having children.
missingStatements.rationale: Grant calls on the state to stop the lines of the unfit through sterilization, and eugenics is a defining policy of the tradition.

notes: Modern science rejects the premise of biologically ranked races. Strands differ: classic writers favored aristocracy and compulsory eugenics, while modern race realists often present themselves as empiricists and stress free inquiry.
